audit.why: Chart reads Ryze / Skill / Pantheon / Pantheon / Ryze / Pantheon / Pantheon and both layers agree, so I left it alone. Ryze's level-1 edge is real once stated properly (Overload 1000 range vs Comet Spear 575); the prose claiming level 1 is Pantheon's strongest window is the half that reads oddly, and I did not flip a stage on my own judgement.
audit.corrected: Left as found; phases[0].why rewritten so the Ryze level-1 edge is attributed to Overload's range instead of a shield he does not have.

audit.whatIsWrong: Spikes were written around 'W root' and 'Q-E root chain' with no numbers.
audit.why: Rune Prison is 11/10.5/10/9.5/9s at 615 range; Overload is 5s at 1000. Those numbers are what make the spike windows actionable.
audit.corrected: Rune Prison's 11s (rank 1) and 9s (rank 5) written into spikes[1], spikes[3], whys[3], whys[6] and breakdown.cooldowns; Overload's 1000-vs-575 range gap written into the late and level-1 text.

audit.whatIsWrong: The matchup repeatedly says 'his Q-E root', 'Q-E root combo' and 'Q-E root chain' — six separate strings. Ryze's Q is Overload and his E is Spell Flux; neither roots. The root is Rune Prison (W).
audit.why: Riot's kit data: Overload (Q, 5s, 1000, projectile), Spell Flux (E, 3.5s, 615, projectile), Rune Prison (W, 11s at rank 1, 615, hardCC + slow). A player told to dodge a 'Q-E root' will hold Aegis Assault for the wrong cast.
audit.corrected: Every 'Q-E root' replaced with Rune Prison by name and cooldown; Overload and Spell Flux named for what they actually do (poke and spread). Aegis Assault named as the frontal block rather than 'E's directional damage block'.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns carried no numbers at all — 'matchup-defining', 'your committal tool', 'your ultimate'.
audit.why: Real numbers make the advice concrete.
audit.corrected: Rune Prison 11s/615, Overload 5s/1000, Shield Vault 13s, Grand Starfall 180s.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'E's directional block' never said which direction, and phases[0].why credited Ryze with a passive shield.
audit.why: Aegis Assault is invulnerable to damage from the front only, per Riot's own description. Ryze's passive is Arcane Mastery — no shield anywhere in his kit.
audit.corrected: Aegis Assault's front-only limit stated in mid; the phantom Ryze shield removed from phases[0].why and breakdown.early.

edits.after: At level 1 Shield Vault plus Comet Spear out-damages a Ryze whose Rune Prison is still a level away and who is farming with Overload.

edits.after: Your level-2 Shield Vault into Comet Spear lands before Rune Prison and HP stacking exist — he has no dash to answer the gap-close.

edits.after: With all three basics you face Aegis Assault into Overload, then Shield Vault in and burst a Ryze who cannot trade back.

edits.before: Ryze is one of the softest level 1-2s in the game and so is your strongest window — at level 1 your point-and-click W stun plus a Q does massive damage before he has his W root to peel you. At level 2 take your W-Q all-in the instant he steps up to last-hit; he has no escape and no hard CC yet. Through level 3 hold your E to block his Q poke, then dash in with W and burst — every trade where his W root is down is free for you.
edits.after: Ryze is one of the softest level 1-2s in the game and this is your strongest window — at level 1 Shield Vault is point-and-click damage plus a Comet Spear, before Rune Prison exists to peel you. At level 2 take the W-Q all-in the instant he steps up to last-hit; he has no dash and no hard CC yet. Through level 3 hold Aegis Assault to block Overload, then dash in and burst — every trade with Rune Prison's 11s down is free for you.

edits.before: Levels 4-6 you keep control: empowered-Q (Mortal Will stacked) out-pokes him, and E's directional block eats both his Q poke and the follow-up Q-E root if you face it correctly. Bait his W root — once it's on cooldown he cannot peel your W gap-close, so dash in and combo. At 6 your Grand Starfall is for roaming, not the 1v1, so use the lead you built to leap mid or bot and deny him the calm farming lane he needs to scale.
edits.after: Levels 4-6 you keep control: an empowered Comet Spear out-pokes him, and Aegis Assault blocks Overload and Spell Flux outright — but only from the front, so face them. Bait Rune Prison; on its 11-second cooldown he cannot peel Shield Vault, so dash in and combo. At 6 Grand Starfall is for roaming, not the 1v1, so leap mid or bot and deny him the calm farming lane he needs to scale.

edits.before: This is Ryze's game if it goes long. By 2+ items his stacked Tear/RoA HP eats your burst, his Q-E root chain perma-CCs you the moment you W in, and his range plus reset poke ignores your squishy frame and shields. You do not out-duel a fed Ryze — your only path is the lead you built early. Force objectives and end before his realm-warp teamfight pressure and root chain take over the map.
edits.after: This is Ryze's game if it goes long. By 2+ items his stacked Tear/RoA HP eats your burst, rank-5 Rune Prison re-locks you every 9 seconds the moment you dash in, and Overload's 1000 range beats your 575. You do not out-duel a fed Ryze — your only path is the lead you built early. Force objectives and end before Realm Warp's teamfight pressure takes over the map.

edits.before: Passive shield + Q poke wins level 1 outright. Identify how Ryze contests the first waves before you commit anything.
edits.after: Overload reaches 1000 units to your 575, so he pokes for free. Rune Prison is a level away — range is his only level-1 answer.

edits.before: Passive shield + Q poke wins level 1 outright. Respect Ryze's Rune Prison completely — the first levels are about banking small advantages, not proving a point.
edits.after: Overload reaches 1000 to your 575, so level 1 is his on range alone. Respect Rune Prison completely — the first levels are about banking small advantages, not proving a point.

edits.before: - Ryze Rune Prison: matchup-defining — His point-blank root — sets up his combo. Bait it. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Rune Prison: 11s at rank 1, 615 range — his point-blank root and combo starter. Bait it, then commit. - Overload: 5s at 1000 range. - Your Shield Vault: 13s. - Grand Starfall: 180s — kill windows only.

edits.before: His point-blank root — sets up his combo. Bait it. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: His point-blank root, 11s at rank 1 and 615 range. Only engage once it is down or baited.

edits.before: Q-poke Ryze to half shield, W-stun when his answer is down, empowered-Q the burst, and E-block the counter.
edits.after: Comet Spear him down, Shield Vault when Rune Prison is spent, empowered Q for the burst, Aegis Assault the counter.

notes: Six strings in this matchup described a 'Q-E root' or 'Q-E root chain'. Ryze's Q is Overload and his E is Spell Flux; the only root in the kit is Rune Prison (W, 11/10.5/10/9.5/9s, 615 range). That is a real gameplay error, not just a naming one: it tells the player to hold Aegis Assault for the wrong cast. phases[0].why also credited Ryze with a 'Passive shield' — his passive is Arcane Mastery and there is no shield in his kit; I rewrote it around Overload's genuine 1000-vs-575 range edge so the stage keeps its Ryze side without a fabricated reason. CHART LEFT ALONE: content win[] and full phases[].side agree with each other (Ryze/Skill/Pantheon/Pantheon/Ryze/Pantheon/Pantheon) but the packet levelChart for this pairing reads Pantheon for the first six stages, and the matchup's own early text calls level 1 'your strongest window' while win[0] says Ryze. I did not flip it — see questionsForUser. NOT ASSERTED: _missing-interactions claims Rune Prison cancels Aegis Assault. Rune Prison is a root, and whether a root interrupts Pantheon's channel is not answerable from the kit files (needsResearch is empty), so I left that out rather than shipping it.
